string.text: Click the name of a setting to see what it does.

Pulls the colours of surfaces towards the middle: dark ones get lighter, light ones darker. Also changes the colour of the highlight on metal. 0 leaves the colour of the texture as it is. Author's value: 0.
Multiplies the colour of all surfaces, both under the sun and lamps and in the light of the sky. Higher is brighter. Author's value: 1.
The roughness the glossiest surfaces get. Lower gives narrower, sharper highlights and clearer reflections. Author's value: 0.5.
The roughness the most matte surfaces get. Lower gives even matte surfaces a visible highlight. Author's value: 1.
How the gloss of a texture turns into roughness. Higher makes most surfaces more matte, lower makes them glossier. Author's value: 1.
The base strength of highlights and reflections on surfaces that are not metal. Author's value: 0.01.
How much the strength of a highlight depends on the material and on the gloss of the texture. 0 makes all surfaces that are not metal shine alike. Author's value: 1.
A second multiplier of the same difference: it works together with the previous setting, the two are multiplied. 0 removes the difference. Author's value: 1.
Makes metal glossier than other surfaces whose texture has the same gloss. 0 treats metal like everything else. Author's value: 0.25.
How much gloss the texture of a metal material needs before it looks like metal. Higher means fewer surfaces look metallic. Author's value: 0.125.
How the light of the sun and lamps fades on surfaces that face it at an angle. Higher gives a softer passage into shadow, and surfaces at an angle get darker. 1 means no smoothing. Author's value: 2.

How the highlights of the sun and lamps fade at the edges of objects, where a surface is seen at a grazing angle. Higher keeps the highlight right up to the edge. Below 1 the highlight gets weaker at every angle. Author's value: 2.
Brightness of self-lit surfaces, the materials that glow on their own. Author's value: 16.
Strength of the highlight on leaves and grass under the sun and lamps. 0 removes it. Author's value: 0.05.
The share of the sky's reflection that leaves and grass lose. 0 keeps the whole reflection, 1 removes it. Author's value: 0.75.
Light that shines through leaves when the sun or a lamp is behind them. It multiplies "SubSurface Scattering Intensity" of the "Flora Fixes" module. 0 turns it off. Author's value: 1.
Strength of the sun's glint on water. 0 removes it. Author's value: 0.02.
Width of the sun's glint on water. Higher makes it wider and softer. Author's value: 0.1.
[ Restart required ] The Disney/Burley model of diffuse light: more accurate, but heavier for the graphics card. Off uses a simpler and faster model. Author's value: on.
[ Restart required ] The GGX model of highlights: better looking, but heavier for the graphics card. Off uses the cheaper Blinn model. Author's value: on.
The least strength of the sun shafts in any weather. Above 0 the shafts show even in weather that has none. Works for both kinds of shafts. Engine default: 0.
Multiplies the strength of the sun shafts after the minimum above. It never goes past full strength. Works for both kinds of shafts. Engine default: 1.
Length of the screen-space shafts: how far the streaks of light reach out from the sun. Only for the "Screen-space" and "Both" modes. Engine default: 1.
How far from the sun on the screen the screen-space shafts stay visible. Higher lets them cover more of the screen. Only for the "Screen-space" and "Both" modes. Engine default: 1.
Extra sky light on your hands and weapon, which are otherwise lit by whatever stands behind them. Less is added in bright weather. Engine default: 0.15.

The number is the spacing between tufts of grass, so a smaller number is denser grass; the slider is turned so that right is denser. The new value reaches the grass that appears after the change: further along the way or after loading a game. Engine default: 0.3.
Multiplies the height of every blade of grass. Applies at once. Engine default: 1.
How far away grass is drawn, in metres. Applies at once. The largest value is 152. Engine default: 152.

Which system draws the sun shafts. Volumetric: shafts in the air, built from the shadows the sun casts. Screen-space: streaks of light from the bright sky around the sun on the screen. Both: the two together. Off: no shafts. Sun shafts must be switched on in the video settings. Changes at once. Engine default: Screen-space.
